tables.heading_context: ## Decision Cheat Sheet: Medieval and Gothic
rows: Small windows are structural consequence plus atmosphere, not lack of ambition.
Vault thrust carried over aisle roof to outer pier
Buttress, vault, pier, and pinnacle form one structural system.
Added vertical load keeping thrust inside pier cross-section
Many pinnacles that read as decoration are structurally active.
Reduced horizontal thrust and flexible height matching
Pointed arches alone do not make Gothic; the system matters.
Ribs guide construction and load paths, but webs still participate.
Empirical height/thrust limits pushed too far
Gothic engineering learned from failures before modern analysis existed.
Mathematical regularity does not mean purely decorative.
Flexibility can be an advantage in masonry; stiffness is not always better.
Pointed arch, ribbed vault, and flying buttress together
Romanesque-to-Gothic is a strategy shift, not just style evolution.
